meta.title: 2026 growth investment: fix retention before adding sales capacity
meta.subtitle: Board discussion

storyline.decision_sought: Approve the 2026 growth investment (the CRO proposes hiring 30 account executives)
storyline.governing_thought: Growth slowed because we lost customers, not deals: higher churn explains 80.4% of the €5.6M fall in net new ARR, concentrated in first-year customers after the onboarding cut. Fund retention first (restore onboarding, €0.8M) with a gated first wave of 10 AEs, for €2.0M a year instead of €3.6M, rather than 30 AEs whose 2026 yield is at most an estimated €4.5M, not the €9M promised.

key_line.message: Growth slowed because churn more than doubled to €7.8M and explains 80.4% of the €5.6M fall in net new ARR; the sales engine kept growing pipeline 18.0% at a stable win rate
The leak sits in the first year: new customers churned 26% versus 12% in 2024 after onboarding was cut to save €0.8M, costing €2.5M of ARR
The 30-AE plan does not hold: with a 9-month ramp it yields at most €4.5M in 2026, not €9M, for €3.6M a year, and pours new customers into the leak
A retention-first plan for €2.0M a year identifies up to €5.3M of the €5.6M needed, with AE wave 2 gated on retention

commentary.title: Why €9M does not hold
points: **€9M = 30 AEs × €300k × 12 months:** every AE fully productive from day one
**Ramp:** a Q1 hire gives about 6 productive months in 2026 (our assumption, note 1)
**Cost:** €3.6M a year fully loaded, €0.12M per AE
**Validate:** ramp of the 2025 AE hires before any offer letter
